aws-waf.label: AWS WAF
aws-waf.sourceNote: action/formatVersion/webaclId/terminatingRuleId/terminatingRuleType/httpSourceName/httpSourceId/rateBasedRuleList/nonTerminatingMatchingRules/requestHeadersInserted/responseCodeSent/terminatingRuleMatchDetails/ruleGroupList[]/httpRequest.*/labels[]/oversizeFields[] are the genuine native AWS WAF logging schema field names exactly as AWS documents them for the WAF logging destination (S3 / CloudWatch Logs / Kinesis Data Firehose JSON log) — the un-normalized raw log AWS itself emits. This is distinct from the ECS-normalized waf.*/http.request.* fields already in this entry, which represent a SIEM-ingested view of the same product; both are legitimate. Added 2026-08-25.

crowdstrike-falcon.label: CrowdStrike Falcon
crowdstrike-falcon.sourceNote: CommandLine/ComputerName/ContextProcessName/ParentProcessName/FileName/FilePath/UserName/OperationType/aid and the *_decimal PID fields are genuine CrowdStrike Falcon Detection Summary / FDR (Falcon Data Replicator) raw sensor-event field names; FDR stores both a hex PID and a matching '<Field>_decimal' companion (ContextProcessId_decimal, TargetProcessId_decimal). Added 2026-07-25 replacing an invented 'cs.*' namespace with this codebase's established 'crowdstrike.*' prefix (already used pervasively elsewhere in the corpus, e.g. crowdstrike.HostName, crowdstrike.CommandLine in src/data/rooms-batch-06/07/09.ts).

fortigate.label: Fortinet FortiGate
fortigate.sourceNote: FortiOS Log Message Reference — traffic (type=traffic), UTM web-filter (type=utm, subtype=webfilter) and SSL-VPN event (type=event, subtype=vpn) log fields, as ingested under data.* by the SIEM. Extended 2026-08 to cover the standard traffic/webfilter columns and again to add the SSL-VPN tunnel fields (remip, remport, tunnelip, tunneltype) used by ssl-login/tunnel-up events; the original generated set only held the subset already in use.

microsoft-defender-endpoint.label: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
microsoft-defender-endpoint.sourceNote: Timestamp/DeviceId/DeviceName/ActionType/FileName/FolderPath/SHA256/FileSize/InitiatingProcess*/ReportId/ProcessCommandLine/ProcessId/ProcessIntegrityLevel/ProcessTokenElevation/AccountDomain/AccountName/AccountSid/LocalIP/LocalPort/RemoteIP/RemotePort/RemoteUrl/Protocol are the genuine native Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Advanced Hunting / Streaming API schema column names (DeviceFileEvents, DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents tables) — the raw export format as Microsoft itself documents it. This is distinct from the ECS-normalized mde.*/file.*/process.* convention already in this entry, which represents a SIEM-ingested view of the same product; both are legitimate. Added 2026-08-25.

microsoft-sentinel.label: Microsoft Sentinel
microsoft-sentinel.sourceNote: AlertName/AlertSeverity are genuine top-level columns of the Microsoft Sentinel/Log Analytics 'SecurityAlert' table. ExtendedProperties is that same table's real column for rule-specific data — Microsoft's own docs describe it as a dynamic/free-form JSON bag ('additional properties that are relevant to the alert'), and built-in analytics rules populate it with rule-author-chosen keys (e.g. 'Query', 'Search Query Results Overall Count'). Because the sub-keys are inherently rule-defined, any 'ExtendedProperties.<Name>' key is a legitimate representation of a Sentinel analytics-rule alert — this is not a fabricated fixed schema. Added 2026-07-25 replacing an invented 'siem.*' namespace that did not correspond to any real Sentinel field. TimeGenerated/Computer/sSiteName/sComputerName/sIP/sPort/csMethod/csUriStem/csUriQuery/csUserName/cIP/csHost/csUserAgent/csReferer/scStatus/scSubStatus/scWin32Status/scBytes/csBytes/TimeTaken/csVersion/Type are the genuine column names of the Microsoft Sentinel / Log Analytics W3CIISLog table — how the Azure Monitor Agent normalizes W3C extended IIS access-log fields (cs-uri-stem -> csUriStem, sc-status -> scStatus, etc.) when it ingests a web server's own access log into Sentinel. Added 2026-08-25.

microsoft-sql-audit.label: Microsoft SQL Server Audit
microsoft-sql-audit.sourceNote: event_time/sequence_number/action_id/succeeded/class_type/session_id/server_principal_name/database_principal_name/server_instance_name/database_name/schema_name/object_name/statement/client_ip/application_name/host_name/duration_milliseconds/response_rows/affected_rows/audit_file_offset/file_name are the genuine column names returned by SQL Server's own sys.fn_get_audit_file() table-valued function — the raw format an analyst reads directly off a .sqlaudit file, as documented by Microsoft. Added 2026-08-25.
